name: Economics (MA)

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.notes:
A master’s program must satisfy these criteria:

• Completing, at Stanford, at least 45 units of credit beyond those required for the bachelor’s degree, of which at least 40 units must be in the Department of Economics.

• Any undergraduate courses taken toward the master’s must be numbered 105 or higher. No seminar courses numbered 300 or above can be counted.

• A grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 must be maintained for all master’s level work. All lecture courses must be taken for a letter grade

rules.name: Coursework toward the 45 units
rules.notes: Completing, at Stanford, at least 45 units of credit beyond those required for the bachelor's degree, of which at least 40 units must be in the Department of Economics.

children.name: Microeconomics
children.notes: They must receive a B- or better grade in course Microeconomics I or course Microeconomics I For Non-Economics PhDs students. All lecture courses must be taken for a letter grade.

children.name: Metrics Sequence
children.desc: Each course in the Metrics Sequence must be completed with a B- or better.

children.name: Complete additional coursework toward the 45 unit requirement:
children.desc: Any undergraduate courses taken must be numbered 105 or higher. No seminar courses numbered 300 or above can be counted. A maximum of five credit units can be earned for a thesis (Econ 400 or comparable MA thesis or dissertation course in another department) toward the 45-unit degree requirement. Whether a course is a lecture (letter grade) is checked by hand; a 300-level course that is not a seminar is moved in by hand.

limits.label: units outside the Department of Economics

children.name: Term Papers
children.desc: Submitting two term papers (or a thesis of sufficient quality). At least one of these papers must be deemed to represent graduate-level work. Usually, this means that it is written in connection with a 200-level course. A maximum of five credit units can be earned for a thesis (Econ 400 or comparable MA thesis or dissertation course in another department) toward the 45-unit degree requirement.

children.name: Additional Coursework
children.desc: Complete an additional two 200-level ECON lecture courses above the 45-unit requirement.

gpa: All graduate students should have an average grade point average of 3.0, which is the equivalent of a B average.
grading: Students in the Department of Economics are expected to earn a minimum of a B in all PhD-level coursework unless otherwise stated.
transferPolicy: Policies related to transferring graduate units taken at another institution do not apply to the MA degree. All units toward the MA degree must be completed at Stanford (GAP 3.2.1; GAP 4.5.1).
reviewNotes: Microeconomics, one metrics sequence and at least three more courses numbered 105-299 make up the 45 units, with at least 40 units in Economics, at most 5 units outside it and at most 5 thesis units of ECON 400. Microeconomics and the metrics courses need a letter grade and a B- or better. You then either submit two term papers, which your advisor checks, or take two more 200-level ECON lecture courses for a letter grade beyond the 45 units. Your advisor also checks the 3.0 GPA, that lecture courses were letter graded, and that all units were taken at Stanford.
